title: Rollout Progression Simulator: prototype playback, failure-mode visualization, and handoff
creator: Lena Park
description: Design and handoff of an interactive "progression simulator" for rollout timelines. The simulator is a visual, step-through prototype that lets stakeholders replay a rollout (canary -> ramp -> full), inject failure modes, and see cost/latency telemetry overlays. Goal is to enable PMs, SREs, and support to rehearse rollback and mitigation flows and to surface UX failure states for graceful recovery. Deliverables: Figma prototype with playback controls, annotated redlines, QA checklist, accessibility adjustments, and a 1-hour handoff workshop with engineering.
discussion: 2026-03-10 - Lena: Initial prototype uploaded to Figma. Playback controls implemented (play/pause/step-forward/step-back, scrubber, speed 0.5x-2x). Visual overlays: latency sparkline, token-cost heatmap. Calling out known technical dependencies: event stream required (trace_id + timestamped rollout events).
2026-03-10 - PM (Rafael Gomez): Likes the "what-if" toggle idea to simulate throttling; requests an additional 'simulate degraded region' toggle to test multi-region fallbacks.

2026-03-11 - Eng (Nina Zhou): Raised concerns about tying simulator to live production events. Suggests two modes: 'replay from snapshot' (sanitized historical data) and 'simulate' (synthetic events). Also notes we need a bounded export format for events (CSV/JSON) and a small adapter service to map event fields to UI model. Action: ENG to spec event schema (ENG-52311).

2026-03-11 - Design review (All hands): Accessibility feedback: colorblind palette for failure states, remove reliance on color alone, add shape/label badges; reduce default motion for users with prefers-reduced-motion; keyboard-accessible scrubber. Action: apply WCAG AA contrast to overlays and update prototype.
2026-03-11 - Analytics (Priya Shah): Requests a 'metric correlation' toggle to overlay request success rate and cost simultaneously. Also wants a CSV export of timeline points for offline analysis.

2026-03-12 - QA (Jordan Lee): Drafted initial QA checklist. Calls out test cases for: playback continuity across long timelines, scrubber precision, failure-injection UI, accessibility keyboard nav, and exported CSV consistency. Suggests adding automated visual regression snapshots for 3 key states (healthy, degrading, rollback).

2026-03-12 - Decision log (Lena): Implement two data sources (replay vs simulate), make overlays toggleable, include a compact summary rail that lists active mitigation steps per timeline point, and schedule a 1-hour handoff session with Eng next week.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype contains interactive playback with play/pause/step and scrubber; speed controls and toggleable overlays present
Redlines document with pixel-specs and spacing tokens uploaded and reviewed by engineering
Accessibility adjustments applied: colorblind-safe palette, shape badges for states, keyboard and reduced-motion support
QA checklist signed off and 3 visual regression snapshots added to the test matrix
Handoff workshop scheduled and recorded; engineering has event schema and mock dataset to iterate against
risks: If live event integration is attempted without sanitization, there is a PII/data-leak risk — mitigate by using sanitized snapshots or synthetic data
Complexity in mapping polyglot event schemas will increase engineering effort — mitigate with a single adapter and clear event contract
Performance: rendering long timelines with dense overlays may impact client-side performance — mitigate by chunked rendering and level-of-detail summarization
